title: Cognitive Dissonance and Behavior Modification
text:
Cognitive dissonance describes the mental discomfort experienced by a person who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values, or when engaging in an action that contradicts their beliefs. This state of inconsistency motivates individuals to reduce the psychological tension, often by altering one of the conflicting cognitions rather than changing the behavior itself.

Methods for reducing dissonance typically involve introducing new information that supports one belief while downplaying the importance or factual basis of the contradictory evidence. Compliance and effort justification are two common contexts where this phenomenon is observed; greater effort expended to achieve a goal increases the perceived value of that outcome, even if the outcome is underwhelming.

The theory has significant implications for understanding attitudes, decision-making processes, and adherence to group norms within social psychological research.
